description:
FOUND s501 (Fable, 2026-09-30) by the review probe written for perf round 38 BEFORE the agent reported (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s501/review/r501q-sigcopy.pl; `.perl` and `.base` beside it in out/).  PRE-EXISTING on main 77212b1f.  SILENT WRONG -- a sub with a signature corrupts its CALLER's data.

    use feature 'signatures';
    sub s1 ($x, @r) { $r[0] = "y"; scalar(@r) }
    my @a = (1, 2, 3); s1(@a); print "@a\n";            perl: 1 2 3      PCL: 1 y 3
    sub s3 (@l) { $_ *= 2 for @l; "@l" }  my @b = (1, 2); s3(@b);          perl: @b = 1 2   PCL: @b = 2 4
    sub s2 ($x, %h) { $h{k} = "changed" } my %o = (k => "v"); s2(1, %o);   perl: v          PCL: changed
    P->new->m(@h)  with  sub m ($self, @l) { $l[0] = "meth" }              perl: @h intact  PCL: $h[0] = meth
    s6(1, $hh{a}, ...) with sub s6 ($x, @r) { $r[0] = "lit" }              perl: $hh{a} = 5 PCL: lit

perl's rule: signature parameters are COPIES, the slurpy array and hash included (perlsub: "the remaining arguments are COPIED into the array").
CAUSE (read off the emission): the scalar parameter is `(p-copy-scalar-arg (aref @_ 0))` -- a copy -- but the slurpy is `(@r (p-sig-rest-array @_ 1))`, which shares the ELEMENT BOXES of `@_`, and `@_` aliases the caller.  `%h` likewise.  The classic spelling `my ($x, @r) = @_;` is RIGHT (rows 7 8 of the probe), and so is an ANONYMOUS signature sub (row 9) -- two more routes, which is the rule-11 smell.
REPLACING the whole array (`@r = ()`, row 6) is right; only element writes and `for`/`map` aliasing over the slurpy leak.

OWNER: perf round 38 (s501q), member #2514 -- it re-routes a signature sub through the lowering the `my (...) = @_` spelling takes, which copies.  The fix must make rows 1-5 and 10-12 of the probe perl's, and a slurpy parameter must not be left on `p-sig-rest-array`'s sharing read by any route (named, method, anonymous, string-eval'd).  If #2514 does not ship, the copy is owed on its own: copy the VALUES in `p-sig-rest-array` (and its hash twin) -- measure the cost on a signature-heavy row first (Air-mass, Perfect-shuffle), the copy is what perl pays too.
GUARD: rows with each shape above; inverse-verified on the base.


=== DONE (s501q) ===
FIXED: p-sig-rest-array / p-sig-rest-hash build the slurpy through the list assignment's construction arm (%p-array-store-scalar / %p-make-hash-entry) -- exactly the `my (@r) = @_` copy -- so no route (named, method, anonymous, string-eval'd, or a signature #2514 does not normalise) shares the caller's element boxes; a normalised signature takes the classic copy anyway.  Fable's r501q-sigcopy.pl 12/12 perl (8 rows FIXED).  Guard: Pl/t/perf-levers-07.t block "#2536" (fails on the base).  ir-spec Â§5.2.
